questions.text: A provider orders testing to evaluate how well gas crosses the alveolar-capillary membrane. Which study best matches that goal?
In DLCO testing, why is carbon monoxide included in the test gas?

answers.text: It reverses bronchospasm after the test
It removes water vapor from the sample
It serves as a surrogate for oxygen diffusion

questions.text: A patient with asbestosis is being followed over time. Which reason supports ordering DLCO?

answers.text: To evaluate or follow parenchymal lung disease
To induce bronchospasm for asthma confirmation
To measure FRC by Boyle's law

questions.text: A patient taking amiodarone needs monitoring for potential lung involvement. What DLCO indication does this represent?

answers.text: Documenting response to a rescue bronchodilator
Monitoring risk of drug toxicity affecting the alveolar-capillary membrane

questions.text: Which patient factor would stop DLCO testing because it is listed as an absolute contraindication?

answers.text: Normal resting PFTs with exertional dyspnea

questions.text: A patient smoked before arriving for diffusion testing. Why is this a problem for DLCO preparation?

answers.text: It can raise blood CO levels and interfere with the test
It causes helium to dissolve in blood
It prevents the use of nose clips during exercise

questions.text: Which analyzer principle is paired correctly for DLCO equipment?

answers.text: Thermal conductivity analyzer separates all gases by chromatography
Gas chromatograph measures only heart rate response
Desiccator column measures FEV1 after bronchodilator
Infrared absorption analyzer measures CO by infrared radiation absorption

questions.text: A DLCO test gas uses helium or methane. What value is that gas used to determine?
A gas sample for DLCO analysis contains water vapor. Which action from the lesson helps protect accurate CO analysis?

answers.text: Remove water vapor with a desiccator column
Use nose clips to force mouth breathing

questions.text: A patient uses supplemental oxygen at baseline. What preparation is listed before DLCO testing?

answers.text: Keep the patient on 100% O2 for the full procedure
Have the patient off supplemental O2 for 10 minutes before testing
Skip DLCO and perform EIB testing only

questions.text: A patient had a nitrogen washout study just before DLCO. How long should the technologist wait before diffusion testing?
Why is the modified Krogh single-breath DLCO technique commonly used?

answers.text: It is the best method during exercise
It avoids all effects of V/Q mismatch
It is simple, non-invasive, and useful clinically
It does not require breath holding

questions.text: During single-breath DLCO, the patient exhales to RV, inhales rapidly to TLC, and then holds the breath. Which breath-hold range meets the lesson criteria?
Why is the first portion of exhaled gas discarded during single-breath DLCO?

answers.text: To remove anatomic dead space from the analyzed sample
To create a positive methacholine challenge

questions.text: If washout gas is accidentally included in the alveolar sample, what happens to the DL result?
After one DLCO effort, why should the technologist wait before repeating the test?

answers.text: To allow methacholine to refrigerate again
To allow test gas to wash out of the lungs
To wait for target heart rate
To let the patient smoke before the next effort

questions.text: A DLCO effort has IVC equal to 80% of VC. Which ATS decision fits the lesson?

answers.text: Accept the effort because any IVC above 60% is valid
Discard the effort because IVC must be greater than 85% of VC
Use it only if FEV1 is 70% predicted

questions.text: Two acceptable DLCO efforts are being compared. Which reproducibility result meets the lesson's criterion?

answers.text: VA greater than TLC on both tests
DL values within 3 mL or within 10% of the highest value

questions.text: A DLCO value is 35% predicted. How should the degree of diffusion impairment be graded?
A patient has decreased DLCO, normal VA, and a low DL/VA. Which pattern best fits the lesson?

answers.text: Restrictive loss of lung tissue with preserved ratio
Obstructive pattern from uneven V/Q or inspired gas distribution

questions.text: A patient has decreased DLCO and decreased VA, but DL/VA remains in the healthy range. What does this suggest?

answers.text: Restrictive pattern related to loss of lung tissue

questions.text: Which value from the lesson represents a healthy DL/VA range?
What is the purpose of bronchoprovocation testing?

answers.text: To measure alveolar volume with helium only
To induce bronchospasm and assess airway hyper-reactivity
To remove water vapor from DLCO gas samples
To calculate TLC from FRC and IC

questions.text: A patient reports wheezing, dyspnea, chest tightness, and persistent cough, but PFTs do not show airflow obstruction. Which bronchoprovocation test may help evaluate airway hyper-reactivity?
How does methacholine create the challenge response described in the lesson?

answers.text: It binds carbon monoxide for DLCO measurement
It measures alveolar volume by thermal conductivity
It increases parasympathetic tone in bronchial smooth muscle
It warms inspired air during exercise

questions.text: Which finding is an absolute contraindication to methacholine challenge?

answers.text: History suggestive of asthma with normal PFTs
Persistent cough with uncertain bronchodilator response

questions.text: Why should a physician be immediately available during methacholine or EIA/EIB challenge testing?

answers.text: The tests intentionally risk bronchospasm symptoms
The tests require carbon monoxide toxicity
The tests cannot be reversed with bronchodilator

questions.text: Which equipment is specifically needed to reverse bronchospasm during methacholine testing?
A patient used albuterol 4 hours before a scheduled methacholine challenge. What issue does this create based on the lesson?

answers.text: Albuterol should be withheld for 8 hours
Albuterol should be withheld for 1 week
Albuterol must be taken 30 minutes before testing
Albuterol is only restricted for DLCO testing

questions.text: A patient used tiotropium two days before methacholine challenge. Which instruction from the lesson was not met?

answers.text: Tiotropium should be withheld for 8 hours
Tiotropium should be withheld for 24 hours
Tiotropium should be withheld for 48 hours
Tiotropium should be withheld for 1 week

questions.text: During methacholine testing, a nebulized diluent is given and FEV1 drops by 12% from baseline. What should the technologist conclude?

answers.text: The challenge must proceed to the highest methacholine dose
The result is normal because only a 20% drop matters at this step
The test is positive at the diluent step
The patient should begin exercise for 6-8 minutes

questions.text: A methacholine dose is given and the sustained FEV1 decrease is 15%. What is the next step if no positive threshold has been reached?

answers.text: Terminate as a positive methacholine test

questions.text: A sustained 20% FEV1 decrease occurs during methacholine challenge. What should happen next?

answers.text: Continue to the next higher dose
Have the patient exercise to 90% MHR
Wait 20 minutes and perform nitrogen washout
Terminate the test and reverse bronchospasm with a bronchodilator

questions.text: A patient has exertional shortness of breath, normal resting PFTs, and an uncertain methacholine result. Which study is indicated by the lesson?

answers.text: A shunt study before every spirometry effort

questions.text: Which mechanism helps explain EIA/EIB occurring after exercise has stopped?

answers.text: Rewarming with bronchial vascular engorgement can narrow the airway
Helium dissolves in blood and raises FRC
Carbon monoxide replaces oxygen in the test gas

questions.text: Before an EIA/EIB test, which baseline FEV1 requirement must be met?
A 30-year-old patient is preparing for EIA/EIB testing. What predicted maximum heart rate should be used from the lesson formula?
During EIA/EIB testing, what exercise intensity and duration best matches the lesson protocol?

answers.text: 40-50% predicted maximum heart rate for 20-30 minutes
Resting tidal breathing for 2 minutes only
80-90% predicted maximum heart rate for 6-8 minutes
Five deep breaths with a 5-second hold only

questions.text: Why does the patient wear nose clips during EIA/EIB testing?

answers.text: To remove water vapor from CO samples
To prevent helium from measuring VA

questions.text: After exercise challenge, when should the first post-exercise FVC be performed?
A patient has a sustained 12% FEV1 decrease after exercise challenge. How should this be interpreted?

answers.text: Negative because only a 20% decrease counts

questions.text: Which post-positive-test action is shared by methacholine and EIA/EIB protocols?

answers.text: Administer a bronchodilator and repeat spirometry to document reversal
Have the patient smoke to reduce CO levels
